GPS, offline location and accuracy help
Understand GPS limits and get a better offline location.

LocalTell can obtain GPS/GNSS coordinates without an internet connection. After coordinates are available, LocalTell uses the offline geographic data installed on your device to resolve the locality. Satellite reception, however, still depends on your surroundings.
Why do I have strong mobile signal but no GPS location?

Mobile-network signal and GPS/GNSS signal are different.

Mobile service comes from nearby ground-based towers and can often work well inside buildings. GPS/GNSS signals come from satellites far above Earth and are much weaker when they reach your phone.

Because of this, you can have excellent 4G/5G mobile signal while the phone is still unable to obtain a reliable GPS position.
GPS GNSS mobile cellular signal network 4G 5G tower no location satellite
Why does GPS struggle inside buildings, even on a high floor?

Concrete walls, reinforced floors, roofs, metal structures and some types of glass can weaken or reflect satellite signals.

Being on a high floor does not automatically guarantee good GPS reception if the phone still has a limited view of the sky.

Reflected satellite signals can also reduce location accuracy.
building office indoor high floor 12th floor concrete roof metal glass GPS satellite weak accuracy
Why does GPS work better near a window?

Near a window, your phone may get a clearer path to more satellites. That can be enough to obtain a reliable coordinate even without internet.\n\nA balcony, open doorway or outdoor area usually gives GPS/GNSS an even better view of the sky.
window balcony outdoor sky satellite GPS GNSS coordinate
How can I get a better offline location?

• Turn on Android Location and allow Precise location for LocalTell.
• Move near a window, balcony or open outdoor area.
• In dense forest, move toward a clearing or a gap in the tree canopy when practical.
• Keep the phone reasonably still while it obtains a position.
• Avoid basements, tunnels and the deep interior of large buildings.
• If the phone was restarted or GPS has not been used for some time, allow a little more time for the first position.
• Make sure the required offline geographic pack is installed.

Once coordinates are available, LocalTell can resolve the locality from the installed offline data without internet.

better GPS improve accuracy offline window balcony outdoor precise permission pack wait location forest dense forest trees leaves foliage canopy woods clearing wet leaves rain GNSS satellite weak signal
What does LocalTell do when GPS is weak?

LocalTell first tries to obtain your position from the device's GPS/GNSS system.

If GPS provides a usable but less accurate position, LocalTell can treat it as approximate instead of presenting it as precise.

On Home and Easy, when GPS cannot provide a good result, LocalTell may offer Use assisted location if a usable network connection is available.

Assisted location only helps obtain the coordinate. LocalTell still uses the installed offline geographic data to resolve the locality.

If assisted location cannot improve the result and a usable approximate GPS position exists, LocalTell can fall back to that approximate result.
weak GPS approximate precise assisted fallback Home Easy network internet accuracy
What if I have no internet and GPS cannot find me?

Move closer to a window or to an area with a clearer view of the sky, then try again.

If LocalTell already has a usable approximate GPS position, it may allow you to continue with that result and identify it as approximate.

Home may also reuse a suitable recent precise offline locality when one is available.

LocalTell does not treat strong mobile signal alone as an exact GPS coordinate.
no internet offline cannot find timeout approximate recent locality mobile signal retry window
Why does LocalTell work well during train travel?

On open railway routes, the phone often has a much clearer view of the sky than it does inside a building. GPS/GNSS can therefore continue providing coordinates without internet, and LocalTell can match those coordinates against installed offline geographic data.

Reception can temporarily become weaker inside tunnels, covered stations, under large roofs or in environments that block satellite signals.

Journey Mode keeps checking location periodically. When a usable position becomes available again, LocalTell can continue resolving the locality from the installed offline data.
train railway travel journey Journey Mode tunnel station offline GPS moving route

No. GPS/GNSS satellite positioning can work without an internet connection.

Internet connectivity can sometimes help the phone obtain a position faster or improve difficult indoor positioning through assisted location, but internet is not required for basic satellite positioning.

LocalTell's offline locality lookup uses the geographic packs installed on your device.
internet offline GPS satellite assisted network data Wi-Fi mobile data
Where does GPS usually work best?

Open sky — usually best
Train or bus on an open route — usually good
Near a large window — often good
Inside a large office or building — variable
Basement or underground parking — usually poor
Tunnel — usually unavailable
Between tall buildings — accuracy can vary because signals may reflect
Light tree cover or sparse forest — often usable
Dense forest canopy — reception may be weaker, position acquisition slower, or accuracy lower
Forest clearing or an open gap in the canopy — usually better

GPS/GNSS can still work in dense forest. Leaves, branches, tree trunks and other vegetation can weaken or scatter satellite signals, sometimes temporarily preventing a usable position. Wet foliage can weaken signals more than dry or light foliage.

LocalTell uses Natural Earth and geoBoundaries / DataMeet India boundaries to identify countries and Indian states or union territories offline.\n\nThese sources provide only the built-in boundaries. LocalTell\'s separately downloaded offline locality databases are not sourced from these organizations.

LocalTell modifications: administrative identifiers and English display names, longitude unwrapping, coordinate quantization, compression and spatial indexing. Original polygon parts and holes are retained; shapes are not simplified.

These boundaries are not a legal or survey map. Border, coastal, small-island and disputed-area results may remain uncertain. Source dates and map accuracy are not guarantees of current real-world boundaries. No endorsement of LocalTell by the data providers is implied.
